hadith_en: Narrated `A’ishah:The Prophet ﷺ recited (the Quran) aloud during the eclipse prayer and when he had finished the eclipse prayer, he said the Takbeer and bowed. When he stood straight from bowing, he would say "Sami’a Allahu limanhamidah, Rabbanawalakalhamd." And he would again start reciting. In the eclipse prayer there are four bowings and four prostrations in the two units..
syarah_en: The sun and moon are two signs from among the creations of Allah - May He be Exalted - proving His Majesty; and they are subjected to His Power and Might.   The occurrence of lunar and solar eclipse is one of Allah’s signs that manifest so we can reflect on the Absolute Divine Power of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ taught us to take refuge in Allah, Exalted be He, with prayer and supplication when these phenomena occur so they end, and the sun or moon be uncovered from the eclipse.In this hadeeth, the Mother of Believers - ʿA’ishah(may Allah be pleased with her) - reports that the Prophet ﷺ recited aloud during the eclipse prayer; so that those behind him could hear his recitation.  It has been said that: this prayer [mentioned in the narration] is the prayer for the lunar eclipse; because it was at night, thus he ﷺ recited aloud.  It has [also] been said: Rather, it was [for] the khusoof of the sun; and that it is the meaning of solar eclipse (kusoof).  And that the words al-kusoof and al-khusoof[which is generally used for an eclipse of the moon] have one meaning; and that is the disappearance of the light of the sun and moon.  Many times, the eclipse of the sun is expressed by the Arabic word al-kusoof, and as the moon as al-khusoof [for one occurring at night].  These two words may be used interchangeably to express one another as well. [So,] the prayers of al-kusoofand al-khusoof may refer to either the sun or moon; and the imaamrecites the Quran aloud during both.Then, ʿA’ishah(may Allah be pleased with her) reports that when the Prophet ﷺ was finished with reciting, he would perform the takbeer when bowing, saying, Samiʿa Allahu limanhamidah “ - [i.e. “Allah hears the one praises Him” when rising from the bowing, and that he ﷺ would say: “RabbanaawalakalHamd” [i.e. Our Lord, All praises belong to You”] like what he would do in the other prayers.Then, he ﷺ did not go to prostrate, but rather he would resume reciting while straightening up by standing after rising from the first bowing.  Thereafter, he ﷺ performed a second bowing in the same prayer unit. Afterwards, he ﷺ rose from the bowing and straightened back up into a standing position; and then performed two prostrations.  Subsequently, he ﷺ rose from prostration and straightened himself into the standing position and performed the second prayer unit in the same manner [as mentioned above].During the eclipse prayer, he ﷺ would bow four times in total in the two-units prayer; thus, he ﷺ would perform two bowings and prostrations in every prayer unit.  It was the way of the Prophet ﷺ to lengthen the duration of the eclipse prayer a lot.The report in Saheeh al-Bukhaaree narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbaas(may Allah be pleased with them) makes this clear, where he relates that the Prophet ﷺ recited [ayaat from the Quran] in the first standing of the first unit for approximately the amount of time it would take one to recite Surah al-Baqarah.  He ﷺ prolonged the remainder of the prayer [as well].  Whenever he ﷺ proceeded to an action, it was shorter in length than what was before it; until he finished the prayer and the sun appeared [after the passing of the eclipse].From the other benefits that we can conclude from this hadeeth is that it teaches us the description of the performance of the eclipse prayer; and highlights the permissibility of reciting aloud in either eclipse prayer [i.e., lunar or solar]..
